sources.entry: Battery Hog - Shows what is draining the battery: live watts, per-app energy, charge history, and drain insights. 100% local. [![Open-Source Software][OSS Icon]](https://github.com/luke-fairbanks/BatteryHog) ![Freeware][Freeware Icon]

summary.one_liner: A native macOS menu-bar and window app for Apple Silicon Macs that shows live battery power draw, ranks apps by estimated energy impact, and keeps charge history, all computed locally.
summary.what_it_does: Battery Hog shows system-wide battery power in watts and memory pressure, with a battery ring and a Low Power Mode toggle on its Overview page. The Processes page lists apps grouped by process, sortable by estimated impact, CPU, or memory, with a Quit button that protects system processes. The Battery page charts charge history over 24 hours or 10 days, built from the macOS power log, along with capacity, condition, cycle count, and temperature. Insights estimates drain rate in %/hr, projected runtime per charge, and overnight wake-ups, and Sleep blockers flags apps holding idle-sleep assertions. An opt-in Agent Mode gate queues heavy builds on battery, and opt-in alerts cover low battery, full charge, runaway CPU, and thermal pressure. The app's estimated impact is described as a relative comparison, not per-app watts.
use_cases: Find out which app is draining my MacBook battery
Monitor live battery watts on Apple Silicon
Review battery charge history and health
Quit apps that are using too much CPU or memory
Queue heavy coding-agent builds while on battery
Find apps preventing my Mac from sleeping
notable: Monitoring is 100% local, reads only built-in macOS tools, and opens no local server or listening port
Agent Mode gate lets coding agents opt in to queued builds on battery, and becomes unrestricted on AC power
Homebrew cask installs are detected and receive the brew upgrade command instead of the built-in updater
Optional password-free Low Power Mode via a narrowly scoped sudoers rule
No Electron and no runtime dependencies
caveats: Per-app Estimated Impact is a relative ranking, not measured per-app watts
Version 1.4.0 must be installed manually once by users coming from 1.3.1 or earlier
keywords: why is my mac battery draining
